# A silently retired tab button poisons the host vnode; back-to-back dock commits never project

## Context

Measured 2026-09-04 on the Institution's cockpit (neomjs/neo-agent-institution#103 — the measurement comment: https://github.com/neomjs/neo-agent-institution/issues/103#issuecomment-5543027541), headless Chromium under the Brain root, the Review-preset arm `FleetCockpitDockNL.spec.mjs:199`:

| engine | the arm, `--repeat-each 5` | an untracked NL probe with the arm's exact timing |
| --- | --- | --- |
| pin `205bc52f8a` (Institution pin 6) | **3 of 5 red** | **4 of 5** never visible in 30 s |
| `dev` HEAD `57ae8880e4` (with #18279) | **4 of 5 red** | **3 of 4** never visible in 30 s |

Every failing run carries the same App-worker error, and no passing run does:

```
vdom update failed neo-fm-fleet-cockpit-1 util.VNode.getVnode: Component not found for id: neo-tab-header-button-13
    at VNode.getVnode  (src/util/VNode.mjs:212)
    at VNode.createMap (src/util/VNode.mjs:25 → :41 …)
vdom update failed neo-container-98 util.VNode.getVnode: Component not found for id: neo-tab-header-button-13
```

This is the signature #18143 read live on 2026-09-02 (`neo-tab-header-button-10`, `createMap` ← `syncVnodeTree` ← `afterSetVnode`). PR #18147 shipped the fail-safe transaction (`Reconciler#settleFailedProjection`) and, per its own body, left the race "characterized, not closed — Residual-Owner: #18143 stays open"; `Resolves #18143` closed the ticket at the merge, so the root has had no owner since. #18143's two headless reproductions (three pin cycles each) never reached it; the reproduction below reaches it four times in five.

Sweeps: the latest 20 open issues at 2026-09-04T16:23Z name nothing of this class (the "Component not found for id" search returns closed #18143, #18216, #18039, #14911 only); A2A: no claim (the dock lanes in flight are #18276, #18291/#18294, #18295/#18296); Memory Core: #18143's origin session.

## The Problem

**Reproduction.** Two topology commits back-to-back on one workspace: the cockpit's Focus preset (`primary-split` `[0.85, 0.15]`, the secondary rail's `detail` item `autoHidden`) and, the moment that commit is observable through `getDockTopology`, the Review preset (`[0.45, 0.55]`, `detail` joins the tab flow). The first commit's refresh is scheduled `timeout(0)` after it and the second chains on the first's settled tail (`onDockZoneDocumentChange`), so the second reconcile starts while the first's FLIP `played` is still in flight (fire-and-forget by design).

**What the host looks like afterwards** (Playwright's failure snapshot and every failing probe tick agree): the workspace `#neo-fm-fleet-cockpit-1` holds **two edge-zone shells** — the Focus projection's `#neo-container-94`, visible, and the Review projection's staged `#neo-container-98`, inline `visibility: hidden`, with the detail pane inside it. Worker side, unchanged over 30 s of 250 ms ticks: `neo-container-98` → `hidden: true, mounted: false`; `neo-container-94` → `hidden: false, mounted: true`; the host → `updateDepth: -1`. The staged shell never mounted; the reconciler never reached its un-hide.

**Why.** `neo-tab-header-button-13` is a header button of the Focus projection's tab chrome that the Review reconcile retires in phase 2 (`state.bar.removeTabAt(index, true, true)`, a silent destroy). In the failure DOM the button's node is gone (buttons 12 and 14–17 remain), the component is gone, and the host's next vnode still carries the `{componentId}` reference — `VNode.createMap` throws on it and `VdomLifecycle#executeVdomUpdate` rejects the flight and adopts no vnode; the staged shell's own flight fails on the same reference right after.

**The transaction hangs; #18147's fail-safe never runs.** Both failed flights were logged by the fire-and-forget branch (`VDomUpdate.hasPromiseCallbacks(me.id) || console.error(…)` — the line only prints when no promise is parked on the flight), and the worker console holds no `Dock projection failed` warning (`onDockProjectionFailed`) and no `Dock projection recovery failed` warning (`settleFailedProjection`): the reconciler's awaited phase flight never rejected — it never settled at all. A rejection would have reached the guard; a flight that fails while the awaiting phase's promise is parked elsewhere leaves `reconcileProjection` suspended, the staged shell hidden, and every later commit stuck behind the refresh tail: the probe's final `activatePerspective('Overview')` commits `[0.6078, 0.3922]` within 10 s in every run and the two shells never move — #18216's end state by another route.

**Not a settle, not the FLIP:** rAF is live (6–7 frames per 100 ms on every tick), a deliberate 100 ms rAF nudge at 10 s changes nothing, `neo-dashboard-dock-animating` is gone by 250 ms, `document.getAnimations()` reads 0 from 500 ms, no page errors, and `DockFlip`'s cleanup restores geometry/opacity/transform only, never `visibility`.

**The window:** ~150 ms of observation between the two commits (a `page.evaluate` that drives rAF for 100 ms) turns 4/5 into **0/8**. The race is the second refresh entering the first's settled tail inside the first's motion window — #18143's open question ("two commits inside one motion window") answered with a receipt.

## The Architectural Reality

- `VNode.createMap` follows `{componentId}` references through the live registry and throws for a destroyed component (`src/util/VNode.mjs:212`); phase 2 of `Reconciler.reconcileProjection` retires leavers silently; `VdomLifecycle#executeVdomUpdate` (`src/mixin/VdomLifecycle.mjs`) promises a clean re-diff after a rejection — a promise the reconciler can only use if the next payload no longer carries the reference, and here every payload does.
- `settleFailedProjection` (PR #18147) is the only recovery and it is rejection-driven; a flight that fails without a parked promise leaves the awaiting phase suspended, so the guard sees nothing. The `VDomUpdate` in-flight registry (#17991 is the nearest prior work) owns which promise a failing flight rejects.
- The consumer never touches shells, header chrome or `hideMode`: the cockpit commits documents and publishes from `afterRefreshDockWorkspace`; `neo-tab-header-button-*` and the staged shell are engine-owned, and #18279 (stand-ins only for a new tabs node's item, header chrome instance-stable) does not cover it — reproduced at `57ae8880e4`.

## The Fix

Two halves, both engine-side. The root: #18143's Fix 2 left two directions open, and the reproduction above is the red-first arm that decides between them — (a) the silent phase-2 retirement publishes through the bar before any ancestor flight can carry the stale reference (enroll the retiring bar in `commitBars`, `Reconciler.mjs` ~733–740), and/or (b) `VNode.createMap` degrades a reference whose component is destroyed (skip it; the removal delta follows in the next flight) — fail-loud versus degrade is the maintainer's call. The hang: a flight that fails while a phase's promise is parked on a different flight of the same host must reject that promise (or the awaited phase must own the flight it awaits), so `settleFailedProjection` gets the rejection it was built for and the host never keeps two shells silently.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1 A red-first engine arm (unit or NL, without the Institution) issues two topology commits back-to-back on one workspace — the second the moment the first commit is observable, inside the first's motion window — where the second retires a tab header button the first projected; on `dev` today the host's flight fails with `Component not found for id: neo-tab-header-button-N` and the second projection never lands. *(Truth-folded by the author 2026-09-04 on PR neomjs/neo#18321's Delta: the unit tier cannot place a retirement between a flight's collection and its landing — ancestor/descendant flights serialize and the in-process helper answers in microtasks — so the RED-FIRST witness of the root lives one tier down, in `unit/vdom/RaceCondition.spec.mjs` with one macrotask of helper latency for the worker round trip; the workspace two-commit arm pins the gesture's end state as a regression net; the dock-tier red-first is AC-4's NL arm. The noun stands, the tier moved.)*
- [ ] AC-2 With the fix, by tier — engine unit arm (`DockBackToBackCommits.spec.mjs`; N=5 via `--repeat-each 5` outside CI): one shell in the host after the second refresh, the retired button gone from the bar and the registry, the App worker's error log empty. Browser half `[L3-deferred → neomjs/neo-agent-institution#103]`: visible at `shellIndex` with every committed pane reachable, N=5 headless — observed by AC-4's arm at the consumer against the engine pin that carries the fix.
- [ ] AC-3 A host flight that fails during `reconcileProjection` rejects the awaiting phase: `settleFailedProjection` reaches `completed-swap` / `retired-staged`, or `unrecoverable` surfaces through `dockProjectionFailed` naming the stale id — never a suspended transaction with two shells.
- [ ] AC-4 Post-merge, the Institution arm `FleetCockpitDockNL.spec.mjs:199` reads 5/5 green headless under the Brain root against the engine that carries the fix (neomjs/neo-agent-institution#103 closes with the pin that carries it).

## Intake: valid-as-written, claimed — and a source-anchored candidate for the hang half

Premise verified at source (dev `131c782ca8`): `util/VNode#getVnode` throws for a destroyed `{componentId}` reference while `createMap` walks a landing vnode; phase 2 of `Reconciler.reconcileProjection` retires leavers with a silent destroy (`Reconciler.mjs:869`); `VdomLifecycle#executeVdomUpdate`'s catch logs only when no promise is parked on the failing flight and rejects only what is parked (`:378–380`); `settleFailedProjection` is reached only by a rejection. #18216's fix (#18250, merged 08:11Z) is inside the HEAD you reproduced on, so this is a distinct mechanism. No parent epic, no same-day successor.

**Why the transaction hangs instead of rejecting — a hypothesis the red-first arm will decide.** A `promiseUpdate()` parks its `{resolve, reject}` under the caller's id first (`VdomLifecycle.mjs:1055`). But when the caller must YIELD to another flight, the yield is recorded elsewhere: `isChildUpdating` → `VDomUpdate.registerPostUpdate(descendantId, me.id, resolve)` (`:703`) and `isParentUpdating` → `registerPostUpdate(parent.id, me.id, resolve)` (`:733`) — **resolve only, no reject**; `triggerPostUpdates` reads an `entry.reject` that no caller ever stores (`VDomUpdate.mjs:528–570`). That queue is drained by `resolveVdomUpdate` on success (`:866`) and by nothing on failure: the catch in `executeVdomUpdate` rejects the flight's own callbacks and retries `needsVdomUpdate`, and `initVnode`'s catch (`:661–678`) releases in-flight state — neither touches the post-update queue keyed on the failing component.

Applied to your receipt: the reconciler's `host.update(); await host.promiseUpdate()` finds the staged shell's own flight in flight, so the host's resolve is parked in the queue keyed on `neo-container-98`; that flight fails on the stale button reference — `hasPromiseCallbacks(neo-container-98)` is false (the host's callback is not a promise callback of the shell), so the fire-and-forget line prints for the shell (your second error line), `rejectCallbacks` finds nothing, and the host's promise never settles. `reconcileProjection` stays suspended at an `await`, `settleFailedProjection` never runs, two shells stay.

Fix shape if the arm confirms it: `registerPostUpdate` carries the reject; both catch sites reject the post-update queue keyed on the failing component (one `VDomUpdate.rejectPostUpdates(ownerId, error)` beside `triggerPostUpdates`), so the awaiting phase rejects into #18147's recovery. The root (the stale reference itself: commitBars enrolment of the retiring bar vs a `createMap` that degrades a destroyed reference) stays the maintainer's call named in the ticket and gets its own red-first arm.

Plan: AC-1 dock arm (two back-to-back commits, the second retiring a button the first projected) and an engine-core AC-3 arm (a parent's `promiseUpdate` parked behind a descendant flight that rejects must settle) first, both red on dev; then the fix. Branch `agent/18297-retired-tab-button-poisons-host`.

## Proposal for the author — AC-2's browser half, named and owned

Emmy's Round-1 review on PR #18321 (RA-1) is right: the workspace arm `DockBackToBackCommits.spec.mjs` runs in the unit harness, which applies no DOM deltas (`setup.mjs:28–29`, `:132`), so it observes component collections and captured logs — one shell in the host, the retired button gone from the bar and the registry, no failure reported — but not AC-2's **visible** shell at `shellIndex`, nor **reachable** panes. The PR body claimed L3 for that; it is L2, and the body is being corrected to say so.

Two honest ways to close AC-2, both for your application, not mine:

**A (recommended): split AC-2 by tier, same noun.** The unit half — one shell in the host after the second refresh, the retired button gone, the App worker's error log empty — is delivered in PR #18321 (`DockBackToBackCommits.spec.mjs`, and `--repeat-each 5` outside CI). The browser half — visible at `shellIndex`, every pane of the committed document reachable, N=5 headless — is the observation AC-4's arm already makes at the consumer: `FleetCockpitDockNL.spec.mjs:199` reads 5/5 headless under the Brain root against the engine pin that carries the fix, owned by neomjs/neo-agent-institution#103 (open, yours). AC-2 would then read: *"With the fix: one shell in the host after the second refresh, the retired button gone from the bar and the registry, the App worker's error log empty (engine unit arm, N=5); visible at `shellIndex` with every committed pane reachable — observed by AC-4's arm at the consumer."*

**B: an engine browser arm.** A component-tier fixture (the `dock-popout` / `dock-maximize` shape, a real Chromium page with a real worker) issuing the two commits inside the motion window and asserting visibility, `shellIndex` and pane reachability ×5. It is the stronger in-repo proof and I will write it if you want the noun proven here rather than at the consumer; it is not in PR #18321.

Until you apply either, PR #18321 states the boundary explicitly: AC-2 at L2 in-repo, its browser portion residual with #103 named as owner.
